display.purpose: Hero headlines only, one per page.

body.purpose: Primary reading copy, ~65ch max line length.

label.purpose: Badges, step numbers, tags, fine print. 11px functional-text floor enforced sitewide.

shadows.name: overlay-lg
shadows.purpose: Modals, the login/auth panel, and any element genuinely lifted above the page.

shadows.name: overlay-xl
shadows.purpose: The heaviest overlay tier, used sparingly for the most prominent floating surfaces.

shadows.name: focus-ring-solid
shadows.purpose: Solid-color focus/active ring substitute (e.g. the lifecycle stepper's active step) used instead of a soft glow, to keep the flat-ledger character even where something needs emphasis.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: Standard button/CTA hover: a small physical lift, never a glow or scale-up.

motion.name: press-down
motion.purpose: Active/press state on buttons and CTAs — a tactile press, not a color flash.

motion.name: fade-in-mount
motion.value: @keyframes fade-in { from { opacity: 0; transform: translateY(4px); } to { opacity: 1; transform: translateY(0); } } animation: fade-in 0.25s ease-out;
motion.purpose: One-time page-load reveal for hero content and marketing-page sections on mount.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The main CTA button used sitewide (Get Started, etc.) — a tint fill at rest, full-strength navy on hover, with a physical lift and press.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #D6E2F0; color: #071B33; padding: 16px 32px; border-radius: 4px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; border: none; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s, opacity 0.2s, transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #0C2D52; color: #FFFFFF; opacity: 0.9; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0C2D52; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: The secondary/ghost CTA — outlined, no fill at rest, plain background-tint on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #0B1C30; padding: 16px 32px; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid #DBC2B0; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s, transform 0.15s; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #EFF4FF; transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-btn-ghost:active { transform: scale(0.97); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0C2D52; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Verified Badge
components.description: The 'verified/complete/done' status pill — Verified Green only, never used for anything else.
components.css: .ds-badge-verified { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; background: #82F5C1; color: #00714E; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 9999px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Gold Badge
components.description: The 'certified/premium' pill (e.g. a recommended pricing tier's label) — true bright Gold Leaf fill, dark text.
components.css: .ds-badge-gold { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; background: #C19349; color: #2A1D14; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 4px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; }

components.name: Ledger Row List
components.description: The system's signature pattern: a hairline-divided list (Trades, Pricing, homepage benefits) used instead of a card grid for any set of 3+ comparable items. Icon + title label column, flexible description column, one continuous unit with no per-item shadow or radius.

components.css: .ds-ledger { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; } .ds-ledger-row { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 24px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid #DBC2B0; } .ds-ledger-row:first-child { padding-top: 0; } .ds-ledger-row:last-child { border-bottom: none; padding-bottom: 0; } .ds-ledger-label { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; } .ds-ledger-icon { color: #0C2D52; font-size: 18px; } .ds-ledger-label h4 { margin: 0; font-family: 'Chivo', sans-serif; font-size: 20px; font-weight: 600; color: #0C2D52; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; } .ds-ledger-desc { margin: 0; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk', sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #554336; } @media (min-width: 640px) { .ds-ledger-row { flex-direction: row; align-items: baseline; gap: 32px; } .ds-ledger-label { width: 256px; flex-shrink: 0; } }

components.name: Overlay Card
components.description: A genuinely floating surface (modal, auth panel) — the only place this system uses real box-shadow elevation instead of a hairline border.

narrative.overview:
First Coast Bids turns dense government paperwork into a clean, verifiable record, and the design system looks like the thing it produces. Sections read as ledger rows: fixed label columns, hairline dividers, one continuous index rather than a shelf of floating cards. Navy is the ink, gold is what gets certified, green is what's been verified, red is what's been flagged. The system is confident and plain-spoken, built for a trade-business owner reading it between jobs, not a design-conscious buyer being sold an aesthetic.

Confirmed anti-reference: generic tech-startup SaaS. No glossy gradients, no floating illustration blobs, no "AI product" sheen. The brand voice is grounded, plain-spoken, and unglamorous-on-purpose; the visual system holds to the same restraint. Density stays moderate: enough white space to read as calm and trustworthy, not so much that it reads as decorative or precious about it.
keyCharacteristics: Ledger rows (hairline-divided lists), not card grids, for anything that's fundamentally a list
One accent color family (navy) does almost all the work; gold and green are reserved for specific, narrow meanings
Flat at rest; real elevation (shadow) is reserved for things genuinely floating above the page, never used to decorate an inline section
Chivo for anything that announces something, Hanken Grotesk for anything that explains something, JetBrains Mono for anything that's a number, a status, or a label

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Navy does the work of "brand." Gold and green are never used as a second/third general-purpose accent; each has exactly one meaning (certified/premium; verified/complete) and appears only in that context.

rules.name: The No-Green-Drift Rule
rules.body: Verified Green is a status color, not a brand color, even though it's used constantly. If a design decision would add a fourth meaning to green, it's the wrong color for that decision.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is reserved for anything that behaves like a number or a state (prices, step counters, uppercase labels/badges). Prose never gets the mono treatment, and data/labels never get Hanken Grotesk.

rules.name: The Flat-Ledger Rule
rules.body: Content sections get hairlines, not shadows. Shadows are reserved for things that are actually stacked above the page (modals, dropdowns), never used to decorate an inline row or card.

dos: Do use a hairline-divided ledger row (divide-y/divide-x + border-outline-variant) for any list of 3+ comparable items, instead of a card grid.
Do keep Verified Green scoped to verification/completion states only, even when a general-purpose second accent color would be convenient.
Do use Muted Brass (#8A6934), not true Gold Leaf (#C19349), for any gold text or icon smaller than 18px/large-text size; true gold fails body-text contrast.
Do reserve real box-shadow elevation for things genuinely floating above the page (modals, dropdowns); use borders/dividers for everything else.
donts: Don't build a 3-equal-column card grid for a short list of comparable items; the Ledger Row pattern already owns that job on this project, and a card grid reads as a second, inconsistent visual language on the same page.
Don't add a fourth meaning to Verified Green, or a second use for Flag Red. Their rarity is what makes them legible as status, not decoration.
Don't use a shadow to make an in-page ledger row or section "pop"; that contradicts the Flat-Ledger Rule and reintroduces the card-grid look the system deliberately avoids.
Don't reach for glossy gradients, floating illustration blobs, or generic "AI product" visual tells; the confirmed anti-reference for this system is generic tech-startup SaaS.
